content.title: About
content.content: Fish and vegetables is a dish centered on tender fish (such as cod, salmon, or sea bass) baked or steamed together with a variety of vegetables like zucchini, bell pepper, cauliflower, spinach, peas and others, excluding carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens, potatoes and tomato‑based sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fish is an excellent source of omega‑3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.
Steamed vegetables retain most of their vitamins and minerals.
The tradition of pairing fish with vegetables dates back to Mediterranean cuisine, where such meals are considered a cornerstone of a healthy lifestyle.
Preparing the dish without tomato sauce allows the natural flavors of fish and vegetables to shine.
A colorful mix of vegetables makes the plate appealing and nutrient‑dense even without bright red ingredients.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Fish provides complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: EPA and DHA help reduce inflammation and support cardiovascular function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both fish and vegetables supply B12, B6 and niacin, important for metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish contains iodine, selenium, magnesium and potassium, which aid thyroid function, immunity and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Fiber and antioxidants
items.content: Vegetables such as zucchini and bell pepper are rich in dietary fiber and antioxidants that promote digestive health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, ranging from skin rashes to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Certain fish species can contain mercury or other heavy metals; choosing smaller species and reputable sources reduces risk.

items.title: Vegetable digestion
items.content: People with sensitive stomachs may find raw or undercooked vegetables hard to digest; cooking them until tender is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, garnished with fresh herbs (parsley, dill) and a squeeze of lemon. Fish can be portioned into fillets, while vegetables may be left in larger pieces or chopped, according to preference. It works well as a standalone meal or alongside whole‑grain sides such as quinoa or bulgur.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked fish and vegetables in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze portions for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before serving.
